subject: [VQueues] Fix tombstones outside horizon advancing anchor
body:
A full asynchronous refill only establishes storage coverage through its last returned key. During the three-way merge, a tombstone for a later cancelled entry could advance refill_anchor past live entries that the bounded storage read had not returned. Once the cached batch drained, seek_after(refill_anchor) skipped those entries until the scheduler restarted.

Treat the last key returned by a full storage refill as an inclusive merge horizon. Overlay additions and removals beyond that boundary are deferred to the next fresh refill, whose snapshot observes their committed storage changes without skipping the intervening range.

Add a deterministic regression for a far-ahead tombstone and an SST-backed test covering the real BlockCache WouldBlock fallback and complete merge order.

subject: [LogServer] Partition log-server SSTs at log boundaries
body:
Use the fixed-prefix SST partitioner to align compaction output with log boundaries by default. Add opt-in loglet boundaries, which take precedence, for workloads that benefit from finer-grained compaction and trimming.

Bump rust-rocksdb to expose the partitioner binding and add a behavioral test that validates actual SST key ranges. Document the new configuration and upgrade behavior.

subject: Allow disabling the VQueue scheduler
body:
Partition migrations sometimes need workers to continue processing partition logs without starting queued VQueue work.

Add worker.disable-scheduler, disables the vqueue scheduler when leadership of a partition is acquired. Disabled leaders use the inert scheduler implementation, emit no new run or yield decisions, and suppress stale VQueue dispatch actions from decisions committed before promotion. Legacy non-VQueue execution remains unaffected, and scheduling resumes after the option is cleared and leadership is reacquired.

This fixes #5193.

subject: Drain partition store opens before processor cancellation
body:
RocksDB open jobs continue running on the storage pool after their awaiting future is dropped. The partition processor could therefore report itself stopped and start a replacement while the abandoned open was still completing, causing lock errors and shutdown crashes.

Keep the restart delay cancellable, but once opening starts, await it to completion before honoring cancellation. This prevents the stopped result from overtaking an in-flight open.

Fixes #4790

subject: feat(ingress-kafka): add SASL/OAUTHBEARER auth with AWS MSK IAM support (#5089)
body:
* feat(ingress-kafka): add SASL/OAUTHBEARER auth with AWS MSK IAM support

Adds an OAUTHBEARER token provider for the Kafka ingress consumer, enabling authentication to AWS MSK clusters via IAM (SIGv4-signed tokens). Configured through the subscription's sasl.oauthbearer.config as 'provider=msk-iam,region=<region>[,profile=<profile>]'.

The provider is gated behind a new 'msk-iam' cargo feature and threaded through the node, worker, and server crates. Token generation supports the default AWS credential chain (env vars, web identity/IRSA, profiles). librdkafka invokes the refresh callback (~every 15 min) on its background thread; parsing is always available and unknown providers return a clear error.

Signed-off-by: Jaiswal, Akanchha <akanchha.jaiswal@jpmchase.com>
(cherry picked from commit ca3b3247d436aae6bc779ac769038abc5f145ab1)
Signed-off-by: Jaiswal, Akanchha <akanchha.jaiswal@jpmchase.com>

* Changes before merging

* Enable the custom oauth callback, and all the oauth codepath, only if msk-iam feature is enabled.

We need this to make sure Confluent platform oauth support keeps working, which is bolted in librdkafka itself.

* Fix tests

* feat(ingress-kafka): unify MSK IAM behind a generic ClientContext and drop the msk-iam feature flag

MSK IAM SASL/OAUTHBEARER support is now compiled into the default build.
The `msk-iam` Cargo feature has been removed from restate-ingress-kafka
(and from the node, worker, and server crates that re-exported it), and
the AWS SDK dependencies are now built unconditionally.

The two previously separate context code paths are replaced by a single
generic `RebalanceContext<T, O>` parameterized by an `OAuthMode` trait.
`MskOAuth` installs the SigV4 OAUTHBEARER token callback and enables token
refresh; `PlainOAuth` leaves librdkafka's built-in OAUTHBEARER handling in
place. The active mode is selected at runtime from the subscription's
`sasl.oauthbearer.config` (`provider=msk-iam` -> MskOAuth, otherwise
PlainOAuth) via `is_msk_iam_config`, so existing OIDC/Confluent
authentication continues to work unchanged.

This removes all `#[cfg(feature = "msk-iam")]` gating and the associated
dead-code allowances, leaving one code path that is always compiled and
selected dynamically per subscription.

* ingress-kafka: address review feedback on MSK IAM auth

- Inline the OAuthMode dispatch in ConsumerTask::run and drop the ConsumerKind enum

- Rename PlainOAuth to DefaultAuth

- Inline the consumer-lag gauge loop back into ClientContext::stats (drop the report_stats helper)

- Drop the unreleased release note for now

* cargo fmt

* clippy

[vqueues] Skip invocation resumption scan if the partition was migrated to vqueues (#5144)
body:
VQueues migration is atomic. Either all invocations have a vqueue id, or none of them do.
As such, if the partition has the feature enabled, it means that we no longer have any "Invoked"
invocation without a vqueue id. Currently, we scan all invocations on leader startup just when
vqueues is enabled, just to filter them all out. So this PR, skips that scan altogether to save
on IO for the already IO heavy failover scenarios.

This fix should be safe across rollouts as well given that the final outcome of the scan is the
same between nodes that got the new version and that didn't when vqueues are enabled (the final outcome
being doing nothing).

subject: [tracing] introduce new ratelimited tracing utils (#5132)
body:
This PR introduces a new crate for tracing utils, and implements its first module which is a ratelimited logging module.

    This allows for an efficient "log at most X times every Y seconds" kind of logging, to help reduce log spam. Prior art on this is folly's `LOG_EVERY_*` macros ([link](https://github.com/facebook/folly/blob/4963d7c505eeb18322eefb35d80a853a3edcaf99/folly/logging/xlog.h#L133)) and LogDevice's `RATELIMIT_*` ([link](https://github.com/facebookarchive/LogDevice/blob/ce7726050edc49a1e15d9160e81c890736b779e2/logdevice/common/debug.h#L272)]) from which this implementation is inspired.

    Usage example would be:

    ```rust
    info_ratelimit!(1, Duration::from_secs(10), field1="test", "my message");
    ```

    This will get logged only once every 10s. The first log line after the period expires will also have the `restate.logging.supressed` field which indicates how many calls were suppressed in the last period. We're also sacrficing on accuracy here in favor of perf, by skipping concurrent logging attempts for the same log line.

subject: [invocation client] relax retry policy and add metrics (#5126)
body:
Invocation client retry policy:
Currently, the invocation client has an extremely aggressive retry policy. Fixed, 50ms forever. During leader transitions, it's expected that until the leader claims leadership, the partition routing information would be stale. The unlucky node that just forfeited its leadership will be hammered pretty aggressively (due to the retry policy) with potentially large payloads until the new leader emerges. This is obviously undesierable. So this PR changes the retry policy to use expontential backoff starting from the 50ms and all the way up to a second to reduce the pressure a bit.

Invocation client attempts metrics:
To give us some observability on the retry behavior, this PR adds a counter for each invocation client attempt, and its result. This required maintaining the underlying error in the RpcErrorKind for better metric labels. To avoid changing the existing error messages, I've implemented a custom Display that maps to the old code. This metric is admittely high cardinality (num nodes * num partitions * num error labels), some labels are rare (e.g. protocol errors) but still it's worth calling it out in case there are concerns about it.

Ingress status classification:
Currently, the ingress' request metric has a status that's either `admitted` or `completed`. We're currently not exposing any metric about whether the requests are succeeding or failing. This PR expands the status label with `request_error` (bad request from the user), `invocation_error` (invocation failed), and `ingress_error` (server failed to to process the request, e.g. due to a non retryable error). This can help us distinguish 5XX caused by a restate problem versus 5XX returned by the customer deployment for example.

subject: [worker] get rid of ghost per partition metrics by reporting per-node aggregates (#5103)
body:
Fixes #4802

When a partition completely moves away from a node, the guages that it used to report are not cleaned (and don't expire) which results into misleading aggregations into the dashboard. The obvious solution is to stop reporting those partition metrics when the partition moves away but the crate we're using doesn't support doing so (see [this comment](https://github.com/restatedev/restate/issues/4802#issuecomment-4613508412) for details).

So instead, this PR, drops the per partition metrics and moves them into per node aggregates instead. Further drilldowns can then be done by `restatectl` or the logs for historical data around partition leadership. This should drop the metrics cardinality quite a bit (even with the new histograms). Those metrics are published from a function that gets called every 1.5s, so it's not really on the hot path. So there should be no perf concerns.

subject: [shuffle] Only report latest outbox truncation idx from the shuffle (#5091)
body:
Before this PR, the shuffle had a 1000 sized channel between it and the PP. This meant it can accumulate up to 1k outbox truncation messages in that channel. However, outbox truncations are prefix based, so you only care about the latest one. To make things worse, the current state was dropping the "latest" truncation messages when this channel is full (using `try_send`), although it's actually the latest ones that matter.

This PR changes that channel to be a watch channel instead. The PP will just use the latest messages whenever that stream gets polled.

To make this work, it required another fix. On startup, the shuffle scans the outbox for the head of the queue. If the queue is empty, it stores the head as None. The head is then later used for truncation from head until N where N is the idx of the command. If at the moment of truncation, the head was still None, it uses the first command it sees as the head. So when it was writing all messages, the head correctly matched the first record written. Now that we're overriding the commands, there's no guarantee that the shuffle will get the very first truncation command it proposed. So instead, we're initializing the head during enqueue if it's not set.

subject: [worker] Change background appender channel to be memory-bound instead of record count bound (#5076)
body:
* [MemoryPool] Add support for overdrafts in MemoryPool

This PR adds support for overdrafts in `MemoryPool` via the `force_reserve` API. This allows the memory pool to issue leases for more capacity than it holds. It also introduces a new `overdraft` API to query how much in the negative the memory pool is. Also, it introduces a new `wait_until_available` which waits until the pool is out of the overdraft mode (just as a notification without reserving anything).

* [worker] Change background appender channel to be memory-bound instead of record count bound

Context:

Before this PR, the background appender's channel was a bounded channel of size 50. This has two caveats:
1. Large commands (e.g. large schema upserts) can inflate the size of this channel in the worst case to 1.5GB (per partition). A coordinated event (e.g. schema change) can end accumulating 10s of GBs of unaccounted memory across all partitions causing the node to OOM.
2. On the other hands, if the append latency is high, and the records are tiny (as shown later in the benchmarks), this 50 records arbitrary limits hinders the batching efficiency quite a bit.

Solution:

The main problem is that the number of records is just hard to configure correctly across different workloads. We want reasonable batching efficiency with bounded memory growth. As such, this PR switches the background appender channel to be memory-bound instead of record-count bound. The memory bound is configurable and will default to 64MB (i.e. allowing the background appender to do up to two full batches per run, though we might want to tune how large we want a single batch to be).

Implementation wise:
1. We're switching the underlying channel to be unbounded channel with a `MemoryPool` on top.
2. Because we don't know how much to reserve from the memory pool beforehand, we're going to allow overcomitting the memory pool by at most once `enqueueXX` call.
  a. To simplify reasoning about the overcomitting, I'm dropping the `Clone` support for the `LogSender`. Otherwise, we might overcomitt by more than one enqueue calls across concurrent senders. We don't currently need it to be `Clone`, so this was a no-op.
3. Once the memory pool is fully exhusted, the background appender is going to start rejecting future appends. As such, the `LeaderState` stops polling the effects stream once the pool is exhusted, and waits for it to become available again. Because leader state has an exclusive reference over the self proposer (and its underlying sender), it can be sure that if it sees that the pool has capacity, it'll be able to send without getting any reservation.
4. As a nice side effect for all the self proposer APIs becoming `sync`, we no longer need to worry about cancellation safety, so the events are handled inline inside `LeaderState::run`.

subject: [worker][refactor] change rpc handlers to return their next steps instead of taking actions inline (#5043)
body:
As part of the work on centeralizes writes to the self proposer inside one scheduler, this PR refactors the RPC handlers to return their decisions to the main PP loop where they get executed there. This is in prep for shipping the proposals to a channel in the next PR.

This PR is mostly mechanical and does the following:
1. Changes the handlers to no longer take the "Actuator" trait and instead return their `Decision` from the function.
2. The decision can be either: Propose a command (with its different modes), reply now, or the pre-vqueues invoker poking.

Tests are much simpler as they no longer need to mock the leadership state. Only meaningful change was a bug in the restart_as_new test `copy_prefix_zero_with_no_version_uses_service_invocation_command` where it was using the default `patch_deployment_id` and it didn't actually hit the assertions inside the mock handlers as it was failing with `CannotPatchDeploymentId`. The tests where not setting expectations on num calls to the mock, so it didn't fail when the call to `append_and_respond_asynchronously` didn't happen. So this was fixed along the way by using `PatchDeploymentId::PinToLatest` to hit the correct assertions. This PR anyways removes `mockall` altogether from that worker crate.

subject: [DataFusion] Fix declared ordering of SQL ID columns
body:
System-table scans do not emit rows in the lexicographic order of their
string-encoded id columns. Declaring (partition_key, id) as sorted allowed
DataFusion to omit required sorts for matching NULLS FIRST queries and return
incorrectly ordered results.

Remove invalid id orderings from the affected tables and the invalid
partition_key ordering from sys_vqueues, whose independent stage scans are not
globally ordered. Cover the failure with a regression test, and omit unsupported
inbox state-mutation entries instead of emitting all-NULL rows.

`sys_journal` retains the partition-key declaration as a pragmatic compromise:
mixed V1/V2 scans can violate it, but V1 journals are deprecated.

subject: [InvocationStatus] Add exact ID selection and batched multi-get point reads
body:
Keep equality and IN predicates as exact ID selections in the DataFusion filter layer instead of collapsing large sets into scan ranges. This lets point-lookup tables preserve the user's requested IDs while range-scan tables can still convert the same selection back to bounds.

Teach the partitioned table provider to group exact point reads by Restate partition when the scanner can re-fetch the exact IDs itself. Use that for sys_invocation_status by adding an InvocationIdSet scan path backed by bounded RocksDB multi-get batches.

Split partition-store inclusive key-range scans into single-prefix and total-order variants, and use total-order scans when invocation-status, journal, or journal-events ID bounds span multiple partition keys. This preserves correctness for range-scan consumers of exact ID selections.

Adapt the worker cleaner to the fallible stream shape used by the new invocation-status scan path, and add scan-mode coverage for the new total-order range variant.


This design delivers 5-10x better performance for point-lookups than the concurrent iterator-per-entry approach that was previously used. This pays more dividends on slower disks and will allow us to leverage async I/O better when we build rocksdb with folly.

subject: [PartitionStore] Simplify and harden range scans
body:
Replace the specialized partition and key-range scan variants with a compact TableScan API that lowers encoded bounds to prefix or exclusive range scans. Use prefix seeking only when the encoded bounds remain within RocksDB's fixed prefix, fall back to total-order seeking for cross-prefix ranges, and turn singleton ranges into prefix scans.

Centralize iterator-bound configuration across direct, background, and transactional readers. Let callers supply ReadOptions so async I/O and transaction snapshots remain caller policy, while short prefixes safely bypass the fixed-prefix extractor and its bloom filters.

Remove the iterator wrapper plumbing, share encoded Bytes bounds across RocksDB paths, and migrate table and storage-migration callers to the consolidated API. Cover inclusive upper bounds, singleton partition ranges, and prefix-versus-total-order selection.

[vqueues] Fix panic on large send delay in eligibility checker (#5017)
body:
Fixes #5011

Tokio's `DelayQueue` timer wheel panics with `invalid deadline` if an entry
is scheduled more than `(1 << 36) - 1` ms (~2.1 years) into the future.

This was causing panics when an invocation is scheduled with a delay of greater
than 2.1 years. This PR changes it such that we park in the delay queue for a year
as a max delay. When (and IF) it gets dequeued, it'll be moved back to to the ready
ring (`poll_delayed`), which when it checks its eligibility again, it'll end up
rescheduling it for another year (or less depending on the run at time).

subject: [df] Fix schema column type mismatches between vqueue and non vqueue tables (#4994)
body:
For future reference, here's an example of a problematic query:

```
SELECT ss.id AS id FROM sys_invocation_status ss LEFT JOIN sys_invocation_state sis ON sis.id = ss.id WHERE ss.status IN ('invoked') AND ((ss.status = 'invoked' AND
  sis.in_flight) OR (ss.status = 'invoked' AND (sis.in_flight IS NOT TRUE) AND (sis.retry_count > 0 OR ss.id IN (SELECT entry_id FROM sys_vqueues WHERE stage = 'inbox' AND status = 'backing-off'))))  LIMIT 250
```

and here's claude's summary to the problem:

```
It's DataFusion's join dynamic-filter pushdown pushing a LargeUtf8 InList onto a raw Utf8 column. The EXPLAIN of the query shows it precisely:

  HashJoinExec: join_type=LeftMark, on=[(id@0, sys_vqueues.entry_id@0)]
    ├─ build: ss ⋈ sis   → key = ss.id           (LargeUtf8)
    └─ probe: sys_vqueues
          ProjectionExec: CAST(entry_id AS LargeUtf8) as sys_vqueues.entry_id
            PartitionedExecutionPlan: table="sys_vqueues", projection=[stage,status,entry_id],
                predicate = DynamicFilter [ empty ] AND stage=inbox AND status=backing-off

  The join key needs CAST(entry_id AS LargeUtf8) because sys_vqueues.entry_id is Utf8 while sys_invocation_status.id is LargeUtf8. At runtime the hash join builds a dynamic filter from its build-side id values (LargeUtf8) and pushes it
  to the probe. But the DynamicFilter gets pushed below the CAST projection, onto the scan's raw entry_id (Utf8). So the filter materializes as entry_id (Utf8) IN (LargeUtf8 ids). When that predicate is serialized and the sys_vqueues
  remote scanner rebuilds it (scanner_task.rs:76 → decode_expr → parse_physical_expr), DataFusion's in_list() asserts datatype_is_logically_equal and blows up. The CAST that would make it legal is lost in the push-through-projection.
```

This PR changes all vqueue strings to be large utf8s instead of just utf8 to match the ones in the other tables we have and get around this problem altogether.

Also made sure that 1.7.0 will continue to work normally against this change:

subject: [Ingress] drain HTTP connections during shutdown
body:
Switch ingress shutdown to a graceful drain:

- Stop accepting new sockets by dropping the listener.
- Ask active hyper connections to shut down gracefully.
- For HTTP/2, send GOAWAY so clients stop opening new streams on the existing connection.
- For HTTP/1, disable keep-alive and close after the in-flight request.
- Give in-flight streams and requests up to five seconds to finish.

Track ingress connection/request futures with a local TaskTracker while keeping
them in the current TaskCenter context. This avoids registering each
connection/request as a managed TaskCenter task, reducing TaskCenter mutex
contention on the hot path.

With shutdown bounded locally in ingress, HttpIngressRole no longer needs the
abort-on-cancel policy.

subject: Add `snapshot` subcommand to restate-doctor: run SQL over partition snapshots offline (#4970)
body:
## Summary

Adds a `snapshot` subcommand to `restate-doctor` for inspecting the data inside a Restate
**partition snapshot** with SQL — without spinning up a cluster.

Today the only way to run SQL over partition data is through a live worker's admin `/query`
endpoint (what `restate sql` talks to). When debugging an incident we often have only the S3
snapshot repository, not a running cluster. This subcommand points at a snapshot repository (S3 or
compatible), downloads the partitions' latest snapshots, opens the partition store + DataFusion
query layer locally, and drops you into an interactive SQL terminal — alongside the existing
partition-store / log-server / id diagnostics.

## What it does

1. Connects to the snapshot repository and **auto-discovers** the partitions under the prefix
   (or a single one via `--partition-id`).
2. **Auto-detects** the cluster name/fingerprint from the repository so snapshot-download
   validation passes (override with `--cluster-name`).
3. Downloads each partition's latest snapshot and imports it into a local RocksDB store under
   `--cache-dir`. The import is **cached** — a re-run against the same `--cache-dir` reuses the
   local store and skips the download.
4. Opens DataFusion over the imported partitions and runs either a one-shot `--query`, an
   interactive `rustyline` REPL (results rendered as tables, reusing the CLI's rendering), or an
   admin-compatible `POST /query` HTTP server via `--listen`.

The tool is strictly read-only: the query engine rejects DDL/DML, and it only ever imports and
reads partition data.

## Usage

```shell
# Interactive REPL over all partitions
restate-doctor snapshot s3://my-bucket/snapshots --aws-region us-east-1 --cache-dir /tmp/snap-dbg

# MinIO / S3-compatible endpoint
restate-doctor snapshot s3://my-bucket/snapshots \
    --aws-endpoint-url http://localhost:9000 --aws-allow-http \
    --aws-access-key-id minioadmin --aws-secret-access-key minioadmin

# One-shot
restate-doctor snapshot s3://my-bucket/snapshots --aws-region us-east-1 \
    --query "SELECT id, target_service_name FROM sys_invocation_status LIMIT 10"
```

See tools/restate-doctor/src/commands/snapshot/README.md for the full flag list and available
tables.

## Available tables

Only the partition-store-backed tables are exposed (sys_invocation_status, sys_invocation_state,
the sys_invocation view, sys_keyed_service_status, sys_locks, state, sys_journal,
sys_journal_events, sys_inbox, sys_promise, sys_vqueue_meta, sys_vqueues). Cluster-wide and
schema-registry tables are not available offline; the leader-only columns of sys_invocation_state
read as NULL.

## Limitations

- Reads the latest snapshot per partition (no older retained snapshots).
- A snapshot is a point in time (its min_applied_lsn), not live partition state.

subject: typo fix
[ClusterController] Proactively refresh epoch metadata when detecting a stale metadata from gossip (#4946)
body:
* [ClusterController] Subscribe to replicaset version changes from gossip

Fixes #4937

Cluster controller now refreshes its own epoch metadata once every
30secs. This is usually fine as it's the one doing most of the epoch
metadata changes anyways. And usually on leadership changes, the
cluster controller is reconstructed and fetches the latest epoch
metadata on startup.

However, if the metadata was updated by another node (e.g. the CC was
isolated), it'll take up to 30secs (the hardcoded refresh interval) for
the CC to notice that change. During that time, all of its instructions
are ignored by other nodes who have observed the higher replicaset
version. In a situation where a partition doesn't have a leader, this
can leave that partition write unavailable until the next epoch metadata
refresh. This was the scenario caught by our jepsen tests in #4937.

Replicaset versions however get replicated to all nodes over gossip
every second. So this commit allows the cluster controller to tap into
this info, and use it as a trigger to refresh its own epoch metadata.

subject: Reduce flakiness of cluster_chaos_test (#4878)
body:
The CI failure is most plausibly explained by recovery after a single
node restart taking longer than the previous 10s
`expected_recovery_interval` — gossip's `Suspect -> Alive` transitions
(5s default) plus cluster-controller leader thrashing can push it past
that bound. This is a hypothesis based on the logs; we have not
reproduced it locally. The changes here aim to make the test
resilient to this and a couple of other timing footguns:

1. Override `gossip_suspect_interval` to 1s in the test config and
   raise the budgets to 60s / 30s so a normal full-stack recovery has
   comfortable headroom.
2. Pre-build one reqwest client per ingress with a 5s timeout. The
   client was previously rebuilt every iteration with no timeout, so a
   request hung against a node mid-shutdown could stall the loop.
3. Race the request against `&mut chaos_handle` in a biased
   `tokio::select!`. Previously, if the chaos task errored out, the
   main loop kept spinning for the rest of `chaos_duration` and
   panicked on `successful writes: 0`, hiding the actual error
   message. Now the chaos error surfaces immediately.

No production behavior changes.

This fixes #4878.

subject: [Resume] Resume backing-off VQueue invocations via persisted command
body:
Resuming an Invoked invocation pokes the invoker (InputCommand::RetryNow) to
fire its pending retry timer. That is wrong for VQueue invocations: a failed
VQueue attempt backs off inside the VQueue (Stage::Inbox, Status::BackingOff)
with a future run_at, so the invoker has no timer to fire and the legacy poke
does nothing.

For VQueue invocations the resume RPC now proposes the existing
Command::ResumeInvocation instead of poking the invoker (gated on vqueue_id,
mirroring the pause RPC). When applied to a backing-off invocation, the entry
is re-keyed to the current record time so the scheduler runs it immediately --
the VQueue analogue of RetryNow.

- vqueues: add VQueue::reschedule, which re-keys an inbox entry to a new run_at,
  preserving Status/stats (mark_transition, not mark_yield) and emitting the
  Inbox->Inbox reconciliation event pair. No-op when run_at is unchanged.
- worker: add vqueue_reschedule_invocation_to_now (no-op while still running),
  call it from OnManualResumeCommand's Invoked arm for VQueue invocations, and
  gate the resume RPC's Invoked arm on vqueue_id. No fencing interaction is
  needed: the failed attempt already ended and the scheduler mints a fresh
  fencing token when it dispatches the rescheduled entry.

[Resume] Generalize VQueue::reschedule to all waiting stages

Following PR review, reschedule is no longer inbox-only. It now re-keys an
entry's run_at in place for any stage where an entry waits with a run_at --
Inbox, Suspended and Paused -- leaving the stage, Status and stats untouched.

The scheduler reconciliation events (RemovedFromInbox + EnqueuedToInbox) are
emitted only for Inbox entries; parked (Suspended/Paused) entries are not
tracked by the scheduler ring, so re-keying them needs no event. For Running
(executing) and terminal stages a run_at has no meaning, so reschedule is a
lenient no-op (debug log) there rather than a panic. This lets the worker
resume helper drop its own stage check and delegate unconditionally.

[Resume] Filter stale run decisions and refine VQueue resume handling

Address review feedback on the VQueue resume path and close a correctness gap
around rescheduled invocations.

- Ignore a scheduler Run decision whose key no longer matches the entry's stored
  key when applying it (run_invocation / attempt_to_run). A reschedule re-keys the
  entry (new run_at) while keeping it in Inbox, so the existing Stage::Inbox check
  does not catch it; a fresh decision for the new key runs it instead. This stops
  a rescheduled-to-future invocation from executing and avoids double-dispatch on
  an earlier reschedule. Deterministic (no clock).

- VQueue::reschedule keeps emitting the RemovedFromInbox + EnqueuedToInbox pair so
  the scheduler drops the stale key and re-evaluates at the new run_at, with a
  TODO noting a dedicated re-key event could avoid the transient dormant flip when
  the entry is the queue's only inbox entry.

- Resolve the deployment patch in OnManualResumeCommand for the VQueue path: the
  command carries the raw PatchDeploymentId (now Option). Writing the new field is
  gated on vqueue_id being set, which implies a cluster min_restate_version >= 1.7.0,
  so older nodes never see an unknown field. The non-VQueue path keeps resolving in
  the RPC and proposing update_pinned_deployment_id for pre-1.7.0 compatibility,
  reusing the shared resolve_pinned_deployment helper.

- Generalize vqueue_reschedule_invocation to take an optional run_at
  (Option<RoughTimestamp>), defaulting to the entry's created_at to restore its
  original priority instead of demoting it.

subject: [Pause] Abort a pre-existing ISM when starting a new invoker task
body:
start_invocation_task registered the new in-flight state machine via an
insert that silently overwrote any existing ISM for the same invocation,
leaking the old task's AbortHandle (it would keep running and could still
emit now-stale effects). Remove and abort any pre-existing ISM (cancelling
its retry timer) before starting the new attempt. No-op on the retry path,
which already removed the ISM before re-starting it.

With the in-memory fencing-token map, the aborted task's stragglers carry the
old token and are dropped by the invoker's is_stale_fencing_token check (the
new attempt was minted a fresh token), so this guards against a leaked task in
addition to the write-time fence.

subject: memory: memory: fix leak from std::mem::forget on leases (#4935)
body:
Summary:
Both MemoryLease and LocalMemoryLease own an Arc (the budget /
SharedState). We used std::mem::forget to withhold a lease's bytes
from the pool by suppressing its Drop. But forgetting the lease also
skips dropping its Arc (and the entire object data), so the strong count is never decremented and
the backing allocation leaks.

Instead, zero the lease's size and let it drop normally. The Drop
guard (if size > 0) skips returning bytes to the pool — same
withholding behavior — while the Arc is released correctly. This also
aligns LocalMemoryLease::merge with the existing MemoryLease::merge,
which already used this idiom.

I also reviewed the atomic operation memory order and it is sound.

The SegmentQueue serializes spilled elements with bincode, a
non-self-describing format that requires all fields to be present
during deserialization. The scope fields of InvocationTarget were
annotated with #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")],

(open, read, decode) and add a regression test that spills all
InvocationTarget variants through the SegmentQueue.

subject: Restore ingestion pipelining with epoch-pinned ordering (#4891)
body:
Fixes #4879

Summary:
Re-enable cross-batch pipelining on the ingestion path (Kafka ingress and
shuffle forwarding to partition leaders), which was disabled by the
conservative #4810 fix that capped each partition session at one
unacknowledged batch in flight (throughput ~ batch_size / RTT).

A session may now keep multiple batches in flight while still guaranteeing
that a producer's records reach the partition log in produced order. Ordering
is preserved by pinning every in-flight request to the leader epoch the client
last observed and processing replies strictly head-first:

  - The client tags each IngestRequest with `target_leader_epoch`.
  - A leader rejects any request whose epoch != its own with the new
    `NotLeaderWithEpoch` response, so a leadership change rejects the entire
    in-flight pipeline atomically rather than appending a later batch ahead of
    a rejected earlier one (the out-of-order append that the dedup
    high-water-mark would silently drop, #4810).
  - On any rejection/error the client carries over the head and everything
    behind it, then replays them in order against the new epoch.

Introduces protocol version V4 to distinguish pipelining-capable (V4) leaders
from sequential-only (<=V3) ones; the client falls back to one-batch-at-a-time
against <=V3 peers. A V4 leader rejects ingestion from pre-1.7 clients that
send no epoch (with back-pressure) to avoid data loss during rolling upgrades.

Protocol / types:
  - Add ProtocolVersion::V4 and bump CURRENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION; route Store and
    Append encode/decode through V3|V4.
  - Add `target_leader_epoch` to IngestRequest/ReceivedIngestRequest and the
    NotLeaderWithEpoch ResponseStatus variant (NotLeader retained for <=V3
    wire-compat).

Worker:
  - `LeadershipState::handle_ingest_request` checks the request epoch, replies
    NotLeaderWithEpoch on follower/epoch-mismatch, rejects epoch-less old
    clients, and moves the ingestion request size/len metrics here.

Client session:
  - Split into `connected_pipelining` (V4) and `connected_sequential_mode`
    (<=V3); carry_over is now a queue of formed batches replayed in order;
    `connect()` waits for and pins the observed leader epoch.

Review fixes folded in:
  - Sequential mode now flushes the chunker's over-pulled record into carry_over
    on every exit path instead of dropping it (was a spurious cancellation /
    record loss).
  - Keep last_seen_leader_epoch monotonic via max() on reconnect.
  - Replace the obsolete single-in-flight #4810 regression tests with tests for
    the new invariant: batches pipeline before ack, and in-flight batches replay
    in order at the new epoch after a NotLeaderWithEpoch.
  - Correct the now-stale ordering comments; fix message/typo cosmetics.

Adds a release note documenting the throughput improvement and the rolling-
upgrade requirement (upgrade ingestion clients alongside/after leaders).

subject: [VQueues] Track per-entry wait stats and error counts
body:
Reworks how scheduler wait-time accounting is persisted, replacing the two
ad-hoc EMA fields with the full `WaitStats` breakdown:

- `VQueueStatistics` now keeps an EMA over all seven `WaitStats` buckets
  (`avg_wait_stats`), applied only on scheduler-driven moves so zero samples
  from non-scheduler transitions no longer dilute the averages.
- `EntryStatistics` records `latest_attempt_wait_stats` and a saturating
  `total_wait_stats` across all attempts, plus a new `num_errors` counter:
  yields caused by transient errors now count as errors instead of yields.
- `MoveMetrics` carries `Option<WaitStats>` instead of two loose `u32`s.
- `WaitStats` switches to fixed encoding and gains `ema_apply` / saturating
  `Add`.

Surfaced in SQL: `sys_vqueues.num_errors`, and
`sys_vqueue_meta.avg_blocked_on_lock` / `avg_blocked_on_invoker_concurrency`.
Entry `Status` display is now kebab-case (`backing-off`) to match
`sys_invocation` conventions.

Note: breaks the persisted codec for vqueue entries, meta, and pending merge
operands (tag renumbering/type changes). Acceptable while vqueues remain
experimental and fresh-cluster only.

Expose the rulebook (#4655) through the CLI so operators can manage rules
without hand-crafting REST calls and raw SQL.

- `rules list [--extra]` reads the `sys_rules` introspection table.
- `rules set` is an idempotent create-or-update: it creates an absent rule
  (DoesNotExist precondition) and merges into an existing one, preserving
  untouched fields with a version CAS (Matches precondition). `--disabled`
  applies only when creating; existing rules toggle via enable/disable.
- `rules enable`/`disable` toggle the soft-tombstone (read-modify-write + CAS).
- `rules delete` confirms then bulk-deletes with the current version (CAS).

Mutations go through `PUT /limits/rules` and `POST /limits/rules/bulk-delete`.
Stale-read conflicts surface as an actionable "modified concurrently" error
rather than a silent overwrite.

Adds client-side serde derives to the rules REST model (the CLI is the client)
and depends on restate-limiter/restate-util-string to parse and validate
patterns client-side.

if partition replication is `> 1`. This means that we will automatically disable trimming and `WARN` the user every
minute that they need to configure a snapshot store. This is safer than the previous default which would keep trimming
enabled (to save space and to reduce risk of historical nodeset decay) but would mean that partitions will fail to
move to other nodes due to absence of the snapshot.

partition table. A todo is left for a future proactive migration for existing clusters with old partition table metadata.

subject: Fix ingested record loss during partition leadership transitions (#4880)
body:
* Fix ingested record loss during partition leadership transitions

The partition processor checks leadership on a per-request basis, so on a
single connection a leadership transition can return NotLeader for one ingest
batch (which is therefore not appended) while a subsequent batch on the same
connection is appended and acknowledged. Because the ingestion session
pipelined multiple unacknowledged batches per partition and, on a head-batch
failure, replayed all inflight batches from the head, the records of a later
batch could end up appended to the Bifrost log before the records of an earlier
batch. The producer dedup mechanism uses a monotonic high-water-mark sequence
number per producer, so once the higher-sequence records were applied the
earlier ones were dropped as outdated and permanently lost. This manifested as
the flaky KafkaTest.callObjectHandler (issue #4810), where a counter fed by 3
Kafka records could end up short.

Keep at most one unacknowledged batch in flight per partition in the ingestion
session. This guarantees records reach the partition log in the order they were
produced, so the dedup high-water-mark never skips a record. The change affects
all ingestion-client users (Kafka, HTTP ingress, shuffle).

This is a conservative fix that disables cross-batch pipelining. A follow-up
will restore pipelining by tracking per-session state on the server side to
reject out-of-order batches.

Adds a Kafka-independent regression test that reproduces the reorder via the
session/partition-processor RPC contract.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Keep at most one ingestion batch in flight across reconnects

The previous fix gated the ingestion session to pull a new batch only when
`inflight` is empty, but that did not hold the "at most one batch in flight"
invariant across reconnects. `ChunksSize` must read one record past a full
batch to detect the cap boundary, buffering it internally. On a disconnect the
cleanup salvaged that buffered record via `into_remainder()` into `inflight`,
so `inflight` could hold two batches; `replay()` then re-sent both pipelined,
recreating the out-of-order append and record loss this is meant to prevent.

Carry the chunker's buffered-but-unsent records over in session state and feed
them back into the freshly created `ChunksSize` on the next connection, so they
lead the next batch in produced order. They never enter `inflight`, so the
invariant holds literally (`inflight.len() <= 1`), nothing is appended out of
order, and no record is failed/cancelled (the Kafka ingress and shuffle have no
cheap retry). Pushing the record back into the mpsc is not an option: it is a
tail-append channel, so it would reorder relative to records ingested later.

Add a debug_assert for the single-in-flight invariant to catch regressions in
any other code path, and a regression test reproducing the reconnect scenario.

subject: Migrate unscoped state and promise tables into scoped variants
body:
The migration logic for moving rows out of the legacy `KeyKind::State`
and `KeyKind::Promise` tables into their `ScopedState` / `ScopedPromise`
counterparts already existed but was unreachable. This change wires it
into the partition store and gates it behind a new experimental opt-in
so the schema bump does not happen implicitly on upgrade.

When `experimental.migrate_scoped_tables` is enabled, the partition
processor's first `verify_and_run_migrations` call:

  1. copies every legacy row into the scoped table with `scope = None`,
  2. commits a single WAL-off `WriteBatch` that range-deletes both legacy
     ranges and writes `SchemaVersion::ScopedStateAndPromise` to the FSM.

RocksDB's FIFO memtable flush order against the partition's CF
guarantees that the schema bump can only become durable on SST after the
copy writes are also on SST. The copy step is naturally idempotent, so
a crash anywhere in the migration recovers cleanly on the next start-up.

Once the migration completes, the in-memory `schema_version` field on
`PartitionStore` (and the copy on `PartitionStoreTransaction` captured
at txn-create time) routes every state/promise read and write through
the scoped tables — `scope = None` and explicitly-scoped services share
the same code path. The data-fusion full scans skip the legacy table
once the partition is past `ScopedStateAndPromise`.

subject: connection-pool: evict idle connections instead of entire authority pools (#4728)
body:
Summary:
Previously, the eviction task dropped an authority pool once it had
been idle for longer than the configured timeout, taking all of its
connections with it. This commit switches to a per-connection policy:
connections that have been idle for longer than the timeout are
evicted individually, and the authority pool entry is removed only
once it has no remaining connections.

Evicted connections are not drained immediately but only
after the last stream that is holding an Arc to the underlying
connection is dropped. Only then the connection is closed.

This is to avoid racing with AuthorityPool::poll_ready.

As a result, a connection may stay alive longer than the configured
idle_connection_timeout if it still has in-flight work.

The corresponding config knob is renamed from `idle_pool_timeout` to
`idle_connection_timeout` to reflect the new semantics; the internal
`idle_authority_timeout` field on `PoolConfig` is renamed to match.

body:
PR #4726 dropped the `service_key` partition-key extractor from the `state`
and `sys_promise` tables because scoped rows for the same service_key are
sharded under `hash(scope)` rather than `hash(service_key)`. The unconditional
fallback to a full partition-key range scan is a noticeable regression for
unscoped lookups vs. v1.6.

Recover the optimization by gating it on an explicit `scope IS NULL` conjunct:
when the user has already promised, via the filter, that scoped rows aren't of
interest, narrowing to `hash(service_key)` is safe. The two extractors needed
by `state` / `sys_promise` (scope-based and service_key-when-null) are bundled
into a single builder `with_scope_or_service_key(scope_column,
service_key_column)` so the call site reads as the dispatch it actually
performs.

subject: Fix tokio panic in vqueue scan when storage tasks finish fast
body:
`for_each_vqueue_entry` wrapped the row callback in `Arc<Mutex<F>>` and
cloned it per stage, but kept the original Arc alive in an inner scope
past the loop. When every storage iterator task finished before that
scope ended, the original Arc became the last reference and dropped on
the tokio worker, triggering `BatchSender::drop` → `blocking_send` →
`Cannot block the current thread from within a runtime`.

Move the only Arc through the loop: every stage but the last gets a
clone, last stage consumes the remaining handle. No Arc survives the
function outside the spawned iterator tasks, so the last task to finish
runs the Drop on its storage thread.

Same pattern already used in `state_table::for_each_user_state` and
`promise_table::for_each_promise`.

subject: [Limiter] Add RuleBook persistent data model and batch writer/diff logic
body:
Introduces the cluster-global rule book that backs the in-memory `Rules`
store of each partition processor's `UserLimiter`. This commit lands the
foundational data layer for issue #4655:

  * `RuleBook` / `PersistedRule` in `restate-limiter::rule_book`,
    bilrost-encoded, `Versioned`. The `RuleBook` is keyed directly by
    `RulePattern<ReString>` — the pattern is the single source of
    truth for a rule's identity, so `PersistedRule` does not carry a
    duplicate `pattern` field. Bilrost map serialisation rides on the
    existing `bilrost_as_display_from_str!` round-trip for patterns
    via `encoding(map<general, general>)`.

  * Soft-tombstone semantics: `PersistedRule.disabled: bool` defaults
    to `false` so an active rule is bilrost's empty state and gets
    omitted from the wire.

  * Batch writer: `RuleBook::apply_changes(IntoIterator<(pattern,
    RuleChange)>)` is the single mutator. Changes are walked in input
    order and accumulated in a staging map; preconditions and the
    `MAX_RULES_PER_BOOK` cap are validated against the *evolving*
    state of the batch. The book is mutated only after the entire
    batch is known to be valid, making batches truly all-or-nothing.
    The book version is bumped by exactly one if the batch produces
    any state change. Per-rule versions are bumped only on
    runtime-relevant changes (`limits`, `disabled`); reason-only edits
    leave the per-rule version alone. `apply_change` is kept as a
    convenience wrapper for single changes.

  * `RuleChange::Upsert(RuleUpsert)` carries a fully-specified rule
    body; `RuleChange::Delete { precondition }` removes a rule.
    Optimistic concurrency is expressed via `Precondition::{ None,
    Matches(Version), DoesNotExist }` on both Upsert and Delete; a
    failed precondition surfaces as `RuleBookError::PreconditionFailed
    { pattern, precondition, actual }`.

  * `RuleBook::diff`: presence + per-rule version drives
    `Vec<RuleUpdate>` for the runtime, with `disabled` rules treated
    as absent. `diff_from_empty` for bootstrap consumers. Hard cap on
    total rules (`MAX_RULES_PER_BOOK`) — configurable knob comes
    later.

Supporting infra:

  * Moves `UserLimits` and `RuleUpdate` from `restate-worker-api` into
    `restate-limiter`. Adds `Hash` to `RulePattern`/`Pattern` so they
    can serve as `HashMap` keys.

[connection-pool] Cap per-connection max-concurrent-streams (#4654)
body:
Summary:
Currently the per-connection concurrent-streams limit is whatever the peer
advertises in its SETTINGS frame, falling back to usize::MAX when no value is
sent. With an effectively unbounded limit, the pool's saturation threshold is
never crossed, so:

  * every request funnels through the first established connection,
  * the pool never opens additional connections, and
  * any load balancer in front of the deployment sees a single long-lived
    HTTP/2 connection and cannot spread requests across backends.

This change introduces `cap_max_send_streams` (default 128) and clamps the
effective per-connection limit to:

    min(peer.max_concurrent_streams, cap_max_send_streams)

That bound is low enough that connections saturate under realistic load,
which lets the existing saturation logic in `AuthorityPool` spawn new
connections, restoring fan-out across LB-balanced backends, including the
end-to-end HTTP/2 path.

Secondary cleanups in the same change:
  * `PoolConfig` is now `Copy` (all fields are stack-sized) and cloning the
    authority pool no longer allocates.
  * `ConnectionConfig` is built once per `AuthorityPool` instead of
    re-derived on every new connection.
  * Stream-count aggregation in the saturation check uses `saturating_add`.

Fixes #4650

a worktree's `.git` pointer references an absolute host path that does
not exist in the container). That worked but dropped the ability to
override the tag via `just docker_tag=foobar docker-debug`.

Restore the top-level `docker_tag := ...` assignment but wrap the
backticks in a shell `if` that falls back to "unknown" when
`git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` fails. Eager evaluation no longer
crashes inside the docker build, and CLI overrides work natively again

just evaluates every top-level `:=` backtick eagerly on each invocation,
so `just chef-prepare`/`chef-cook`/`build`/... called inside the docker
build context triggered `git rev-parse` against the copied `.git`. In a
git worktree, `.git` is a pointer file with an absolute host path that
does not exist inside the container, causing "not a git repository" and
failing the planner stage of `just docker-debug`.

Move the tag computation into a `_docker-tag` recipe invoked from the
`docker`, `docker-debug`, and `docker-local-fedora` recipes, so git is
only consulted on the host when building an image.

## sys_vqueue_meta

- New partitioned datafusion table surfacing per-vqueue identity, lifecycle flags/timestamps, EMA durations, and per-stage counts from `VQueueMeta`.
- New `ScanVQueueMetaTable` trait in `storage-api`, implemented on `PartitionStore` at `Priority::Low`; decode uses `VQueueMetaRef` via bilrost `decode_borrowed` for zero-copy string columns.

## Wait-time accounting

- `Stats` rewritten around a single `Option<(WaitBucket, Instant)>` + `EnumMap` accumulator. *At most one open wait segment* is now a structural invariant, fixing over-attribution on resource transitions.
- One `set_wait()` entry point; `finalize()` / `snapshot()` share one builder; `reset()` flushes open segments so preempted items still contribute to node-wide counters.
- `ResourceKind -> WaitBucket` mapping is exhaustive — new variants are a compile error until a bucket is assigned.
- Node-level invoker throttling is one bucket whether observed as `BlockedOn` or as a token-bucket delay.

## EMAs

- Two new `VQueueStatistics` fields sampled on **every** `Inbox -> Running` transition (retries included): `avg_blocked_on_concurrency_rules_ms`, `avg_blocked_on_invoker_throttling_ms`.
- Carried through `MoveMetrics`; surfaced as two `Duration` columns on `sys_vqueue_meta`.
- Aspirational per-entry wait-time todo in `EntryStatistics` removed — vqueue-level EMA preferred over per-entry signal that decays in relevance.

## Naming

- `WaitStats` fields uniformly use `blocked_on_*_ms`; metric constants/strings follow `VQUEUE_<X>_WAIT_MS` / `restate.vqueue.scheduler.<x>_wait_ms.total`; `WaitBucket` and `ResourceKind` variants use matching names.
- Pre-existing metric-string / describe-text inconsistencies fixed.
- Bilrost tag numbers preserved on renamed fields — wire-compatible.

The `inactivity_timeout` in the v4 protocol runner's bidi-stream loop was
recreated as a fresh `tokio::time::sleep` future on every `tokio::select!`

Signal and invocation-response commands from ingress RPCs are now appended
to Bifrost without dedup information. Without dedup, these records are never
filtered by the epoch-based deduplication mechanism during leadership
transitions, which previously caused accepted signals to be silently
dropped.

subject: Fix stale reads on non-leader partition processors for mutation RPCs
body:
RPC handlers for restart_as_new, resume, and pause invocations read from
local storage without checking leadership first. On a follower with stale
storage (common during leader transitions in multi-node clusters), the
invocation appears as Free, returning NotFound (404) instead of NotLeader
(503). Since clients only retry on 503, this causes flaky test failures.

Add leader guards matching the existing pattern in get_invocation_output,
returning NotLeader when the partition processor is not the leader so the
request gets retried on the actual leader.

Fixes restatedev/restate#4587

subject: Fix missed-notification race in BudgetedStateStream
body:
The BudgetedStateStream created its AvailabilityNotified future AFTER
try_reserve failed, leaving a window where concurrent notify_waiters()
calls (from other invocations returning memory) were silently lost.
Since notify_waiters() only wakes registered waiters and does not store
permits, the stream could get stuck in Poll::Pending indefinitely.

This manifested as a stuck readState invocation in the
InvokerMemoryTest e2e test under the alwaysSuspending configuration:
49/50 virtual object invocations completed, but the last one's
BudgetedStateStream missed all return-memory notifications and blocked
forever waiting for budget, holding 32 KiB of pool memory.

Fix by creating the notification future BEFORE try_reserve (matching
the proven pattern in LocalMemoryPool::reserve and PollMemoryPool),
so any concurrent notify_waiters() during or after the reserve check
is guaranteed to wake the stream.

Closes restatedev/restate#4575

unreachable nodes, return results from the available nodes instead of failing the
entire query. Per-node errors are surfaced as structured warnings alongside the
partial result set.

- QueryContext::execute() returns a QueryResult that bundles the record batch

  extract them from any NodeFanOutExecutionPlan nodes.
- QueryWarningStream in the gRPC handler buffers the last response and attaches
  accumulated warnings to it before yielding, piggybacking on existing data
  rather than sending a trailing empty message.

subject: Support dual-stack by defaulting bind-ip to :: instead of 0.0.0.0 (#4529)
body:
Change the default bind address from 0.0.0.0 (IPv4 only) to :: (IPv6
unspecified), which creates a dual-stack socket accepting both IPv4 and
IPv6 connections on most systems.

This fixes two problems:
- In IPv6-only environments (e.g. K8s clusters), 0.0.0.0 fails to bind
  entirely because no IPv4 stack is available.
- In dual-stack environments where DNS resolves peer addresses to IPv6,
  nodes were unreachable because the server only listened on IPv4.

Also add an IPv6-first probe to the routable IP detection so that
advertised addresses are correctly derived in IPv6-only environments,
falling back to IPv4 when IPv6 is not available. The IPv6 probe uses
Cloudflare's 2606:4700:4700::1111, consistent with the IPv4 probe's
use of 1.1.1.1.

This fixes #4529.

subject: Fix is_out_of_memory livelock via pinned memory tracking
body:
Introduce PinnableMemoryStream trait so consumers that merge leases can
signal non-reclaimable (pinned) memory back to the budgeted stream:

- Add pinned parameter to LocalMemoryPool::reserve() and is_out_of_memory()
  Formula: reclaimable = (capacity - pinned) + min(global, upper_bound - capacity)
- PinnableMemoryStream trait with pin_memory/unpin_memory (crates/memory)
- IgnorePinnableMemoryStream: no-op wrapper for streams without budgets
- PinnableMapErr: error-mapping adapter preserving PinnableMemoryStream
- BudgetedStateStream: proper struct-based Stream impl with inline
  AvailabilityNotified (pin-project, no heap allocation), pinned as plain
  usize, and split-based lease handoff
- LocalMemoryPooledStateStream now returns (Bytes, Bytes, LocalMemoryLease)
  triples and requires PinnableMemoryStream bound
- OutOfMemory::needed includes pinned so callers know total requirement
- collect_eager_state calls pin_memory after each lease merge

(Shared+outbound split: ResponseStream/DecoderStream pinning will be
applied with the inbound memory budgeting commits.)

subject: Replace InvokerBody with Bytes::from_owner to fix outbound budget deadlock
body:
InvokerBody held the previous frame's memory lease in current_lease until
the next frame arrived. This created a circular dependency: sending frame
N+1 required outbound budget held by frame N's lease, which was only
released when frame N+1 was received — a deadlock that caused invocations
to get stuck in 'running' state with reserve().await blocking forever
inside a select! branch, preventing inactivity timeouts from firing.

Fix: embed the LocalMemoryLease inside the Bytes data via
Bytes::from_owner(LeasedBytes { data, _lease }). The lease now lives
exactly as long as hyper holds the bytes. When hyper drops the data
after sending on the wire, the lease is automatically released. This
eliminates the circular dependency entirely.

- Remove InvokerBody struct, impl Body, impl Unpin, bounds assertion
- Add LeasedBytes wrapper + leased_frame() helper
- Replace InvokerBody with StreamBody<UnboundedReceiverStream<...>>
- Simplify InvokerBodySender channel from (Frame, Option<Lease>) to
  Result<Frame<Bytes>, Infallible>
- Update write_with_lease/write_raw_with_lease in both protocol runners

subject: [Memory] Replace polling timeout with global pool notification in LocalMemoryPool::reserve
body:
Replace the 500ms FEASIBILITY_RECHECK_INTERVAL sleep in reserve() with
a proper notification from the global MemoryPool. When the local budget
cannot satisfy a reservation, reserve() now select!s on both the local
SharedState::notify (fires on local in-flight lease drops) and the
global pool's availability_notified() (fires when any consumer returns
memory to the global pool). This eliminates up to 500ms of latency.

Also fixes a subtle notification ordering issue: both Notified futures
are now created before try_reserve(), preventing a missed wakeup if
memory is freed between the check and the subscribe.

delete_journal used the notification-id prefix (jn) instead of the
completion-id prefix (jc) when cleaning up JournalCompletionIdToCommandIndex
entries, causing them to never be deleted when journals were purged.

Additionally, a non-blocking background cleanup task now runs on first
startup after upgrade to remove any orphaned jc entries that accumulated
due to this bug. The task processes entries one invocation at a time to
avoid unbounded memory usage and is tracked via an FSM flag so it only
runs once per partition store. Fresh partition stores are marked as
already clean to skip the unnecessary scan.

Address review feedback for jc orphan cleanup

- Add cancellation support: check predicate at invocation boundaries,

Gate the ReplyIfNotReady point-read in GetInvocationOutput on leadership
to prevent non-leader partition processors from serving stale data. A
follower whose local store has not yet replayed all log entries could
return NotFound (HTTP 404) for an invocation that actually exists on the
leader. By returning NotLeader instead, the ingress retry loop retries

subject: [Invoker] Convert notifications/completions to signal-only delivery
body:
The partition processor now sends only entry indexes (signals) to the
invoker instead of full data payloads for completions and notifications.
The invocation task reads the actual data from RocksDB on-demand during
the bidi-stream phase.

Key changes:
- Add read_journal_entry() non-transactional point read to InvocationReader
- Notification enum carries only entry indexes, not data payloads
- Update InvokerHandle, InputCommand, Action::ForwardCompletion/Notification
- Clone InvocationReader before transaction for bidi-phase reads
- Both protocol runners read from storage on notification signal
- Update all test matchers for signal-only assertions

[Invoker] Fix signal-only completion/notification delivery issues

Address review feedback on the signal-only notification PR:

1. Replace anyhow::Error with associated type on InvocationReader trait
   - Add Error associated type to InvocationReader (matching the
     existing pattern in InvocationReaderTransaction)
   - Use InvokerStorageReaderError in the real impl, Infallible in tests
   - Remove anyhow dependency from restate-invoker-api

2. Hardcode using_journal_table_v2=false in v1-v3 protocol runner
   - The v1-v3 runner is already guarded against journal table v2
     (errors with DeploymentDeprecated), so passing the metadata flag
     is misleading. Hardcode false in read_completion_from_storage.

3. Use CompletionResultExtractor instead of CompletionMessage for
   extracting completion results from journal entry bytes
   - CompletionMessage has uint32 entry_index at tag 1, which causes
     a prost wire-type mismatch when decoding entries that have
     length-delimited fields at tag 1 (e.g. GetStateEntryMessage's
     bytes key field).
   - CompletionResultExtractor has only the result oneof (tags 13/14/15)
     so unknown entry-specific fields are safely skipped by prost.

4. Store completion result before forward_completion in fallback paths
   - 5 code paths called forward_completion without first writing
     the completion into the entry bytes via write_completion.
     In signal-only mode, the invoker reads the entry from RocksDB,
     so the completion must be present in the stored bytes.
   - Affected: GetState (no keyed service), GetPromise/PeekPromise/
     CompletePromise (no promises), GetCallInvocationId (callee missing)

5. Update comment at GetCallInvocationId else branch to reflect
   the signal-only forwarding design.

subject: Add configurable eager state size limit and unify eager state controls
body:
Add a new 'eager-state-size-limit' configuration option (ByteCount, 0-able)
that caps the total byte size of state entries sent eagerly in the
StartMessage. When exceeded, partial state is sent and the service fetches
remaining keys lazily. Set to '0' to disable eager state entirely.

Defaults to message-size-limit when unset and is always clamped to it.

Key changes:

- Config type is ByteCount (allows 0) resolved and clamped at config load
  time via InvokerOptions::merge(). InvocationTask stores a concrete usize.
- Schema-level types (ServiceRevision, Handler, ServiceMetadata,
  HandlerMetadata, InvocationAttemptOptions) use Option<ByteCount> for
  per-service/per-handler overrides. REST API exposes it as Option<String>.
- Fuse legacy 'enable_lazy_state: true' into ByteCount::ZERO during
  resolution, and deprecated 'disable_eager_state' into ByteCount::ZERO
  during config merge (with a warning on conflicting settings).
- Extract collect_eager_state() helper that collects state entries up to the
  size limit. If even the first entry exceeds the limit, no eager state is
  sent (partial flag set, empty entries).
- Add 'restate.invoker.eager_state_truncated.total' counter metric for
  operational visibility when the limit is hit.
- Add unit tests for collect_eager_state covering truncation, partial flag
  propagation, boundary conditions, and error propagation.

This fixes #4345.

body:
Address review feedback on storage compact command

Fix InvocationError metadata lost during protobuf deserialization of ResponseResult
body:
The TryFrom<ResponseResult> implementation for deserializing a
ResponseResult from protobuf storage was constructing an InvocationError
with only code and message, silently dropping the failure_metadata field.
The serialization direction (From<ResponseResult>) correctly included
failure_metadata, so metadata was written to storage but lost on read.

This surfaces in multi-node clusters when an idempotent invocation
completes on one node and the result is later read back from storage on
another. For example, in the threeNodes/UserErrors test: the ingress on
N1 submits callTerminallyFailingCall, but partition 0 is reassigned to
N3 mid-flight. N3 replays the log, completes the invocation, and
persists the completed status (with metadata) to RocksDB. When N1's
ingress retries (using the idempotency key), N3's partition processor
finds InvocationStatus::Completed in storage and returns the stored
response_result — which goes through the buggy TryFrom<ResponseResult>
deserialization, stripping the metadata before it reaches the ingress.

This fixes #4508.

subject: [LogServer][4/N] Rework RocksDB tuning for log-server workload
body:
Rework the log-server RocksDB configuration to better match its actual
workload: write-heavy append-only data with rare reads (served by the
RecordCache) and tiny metadata updates via merge operators.

Key changes:

Enable atomic_flush for cross-CF consistency:
  Both CFs now flush atomically, ensuring trim points/seals and data
  records are always consistent on disk. This removes the need for WAL
  replay to reconstruct the relationship between CFs after a crash.
  Replaces enable_pipelined_write which is incompatible with
  atomic_flush and carried known risks (history of deadlocks/stalls)
  with minimal benefit given the single-writer batch pattern.

Delay data CF compaction to benefit from trimming:
  Raise level0_file_num_compaction_trigger from 2 to 8. With the
  RecordCache absorbing most reads, higher L0 read amplification is
  acceptable, and delaying compaction gives trim operations time to
  reclaim data before it gets compacted deeper into the LSM tree —
  reducing write amplification. Comfortable headroom remains to the
  default slowdown (20) and stop (36) triggers.

Per-CF tuning instead of shared defaults:
  The data and metadata CFs now have independently tuned options
  reflecting their fundamentally different workload profiles:

  Data CF (append-only, write-heavy, sequential scans):
  - min_write_buffer_number_to_merge=1 (forced by atomic_flush, and
    correct for append-only — no dedup benefit from merging)
  - level0_file_num_compaction_trigger=8, max_bytes_for_level_base=2×budget
  - optimize_filters_for_hits=false (need last-level bloom filters
    because DeleteRange tombstones from trimming can cause misses)
  - 64KiB block size (benefits sequential prefix scans)

  Metadata CF (tiny, point lookups, merge operators):
  - write_buffer_size matches data CF to prevent triggering atomic
    flushes independently (actual memory use is negligible)
  - Eager compaction (trigger=2) since metadata compactions are free
  - 4KiB block size (appropriate for point lookups on small values)
  - Compression fully disabled (negligible disk savings, avoids CPU
    overhead)
  - max_successive_merges disabled (merge op is a trivial max() on
    8-byte offsets, chains bounded by flush frequency)

Dynamic config updates narrowed to data CF:
  The metadata CF budget is a fixed constant (8MiB), so live config
  updates only adjust the data CF. The metadata CF write_buffer_size
  is kept in sync with the data CF to maintain the atomic_flush
  invariant.

subject: [Futures-Util] Add monotonic_token and waiter_queue modules
body:
Extract two generic, reusable utilities into restate-futures-util:

**monotonic_token**: A lightweight mechanism for a producer to signal
completion of a prefix of sequentially issued work items. Provides
Token<T>, TokenOwner<T>, Tokens<T>, and TokenListener<T> types with
a phantom type parameter to prevent mixing tokens from different domains.
Uses atomics (Relaxed/Release/Acquire) for lock-free operation — no
RwLock or watch overhead.

**waiter_queue**: A priority-drainable queue (WaiterQueue<K, V>) designed
for the common case where entries arrive in key-order. Uses an adaptive
strategy: push_back for in-order inserts (O(1)), binary-search insert for
out-of-order (rare). Drain is always a simple front-pop. Includes a
Criterion benchmark comparing four strategies (naive, compact,
adaptive, sorted-insert).

Both modules include comprehensive documentation and tests. Neither
references any specific use-case — they are general-purpose building
blocks.

subject: [Bifrost] Use adaptive timeouts for all replicated-loglet tasks
[Bifrost] Use adaptive timeouts for appends
body:
Previously the sequencer used a fixed store timeout (configurable via
`rpc_timeout`) for every append wave, regardless of actual network
conditions. A timeout set too conservatively wastes time waiting for
genuinely slow or failed nodes; one set too aggressively causes spurious
timeouts during transient slowdowns.

This change wires in the [adaptive-timeout](https://github.com/AhmedSoliman/adaptive-timeout)
crate so that the effective timeout adjusts automatically based on
observed per-node store latencies.

## How it works

A store-focused `LatencyTracker` records round-trip times for every store
RPC (on success, on timeout, and on drop). The tracker maintains a
per-node sliding-window histogram (60 s window, 10 sub-windows) backed
by HdrHistogram, so old data ages out gradually rather than all at once.

When starting a new append wave, `AdaptiveTimeout::select_timeout` is
called with the set of target nodes. For each destination it queries the
P99.99 of recent latencies and computes:

    timeout = clamp(safety_factor × P99.99 × 2^(attempt-1), min, max)

The wave timeout is the **maximum** across all target nodes, so it is
generous enough for the slowest expected peer. The `store_timeout`
config field becomes the [min, max] clamp range rather than a fixed
value.

Two `AdaptiveTimeout` instances are used with different safety factors:

- **Wave timeout** (safety_factor=2.0): 2× headroom over the observed
  quantile gives the log-servers enough runway to actually persist the
  records before we give up and retry.
- **Inter-wave backoff** (safety_factor=1.0): the delay between retry
  waves tracks the same latency distribution but without extra headroom,
  keeping the retry cadence tight.

On cold start or sparse traffic (fewer than `min_samples` observations)
the algorithm falls back gracefully to pure exponential backoff from the
configured minimum timeout.

## Configuration syntax

`store_timeout` is now a `BackoffInterval` expressed as a compact
duration-range string `"<min>..<max>"`, for example:

    bifrost.replicated-loglet.rpc-timeout = "250ms..15s"

This single string captures the full shape of the exponential backoff
envelope: the initial timeout (floor), the ceiling after which retries
stop growing, and — implicitly through the adaptive algorithm — the
doubling behaviour in between. Duration units follow jiff's friendly
format (`ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`, and verbose forms); fractional values
such as `0.5s` are also accepted. The previous `sequencer_retry_policy`
field is deprecated in favour of this simpler spelling.

SessionManagerInner caches SessionHandles in a DashMap that is never
cleaned up. If a PartitionSession background task terminates (e.g. due
to ConnectError::Shutdown or cancellation), the cached handle becomes
permanently stale — every subsequent ingest() call for that partition
returns SessionClosed forever.

mpsc sender) before returning it from SessionManagerInner::get(). When
a stale handle is detected, it is evicted from the cache and a fresh
session is started transparently.

body:
Previously, concurrency permits were stored directly in Entry objects
and released when the Decision was dropped. This caused permit leaks
when items were killed/cancelled before being run, as the permits would
be lost without being properly returned to the pool.

This change moves permit storage to a pending_permits HashMap in the
scheduler. Permits are now explicitly retrieved via pop_permit() when
the leader actually runs an item, and properly released on rejection
or removal events.

Additionally, when an item removal invalidates the queue head, we now
remove the queue from the eligibility tracker state (even if it remains
in the ready ring) and force a membership refresh to recalculate its
eligibility. Previously this could cause a crash because the queue
state was not reset to NeedsPoll after head invalidation.

Changes:
- Move permit storage from Entry to DRRScheduler.pending_permits
- Add pop_permit() method to retrieve permits when running items
- Release permits on RunAttemptRejected and Removed events
- Reset eligibility state on head invalidation from item removal
- Handle missing eligibility state gracefully in next_eligible()
- Update tests to explicitly pop permits to simulate leader behavior

subject: Introduce version barrier for enabling journal v2 by default
body:
The version barrier requiring min Restate version v1.6.0 will enable the
journal v2 by default. It will be written when becoming leader and running
at least v1.7.0.

Writing the journal v2 by default changes the logic of the state machine. That's
why we are guarding it with a version barrier so that during a rolling upgrade the
state machine state won't diverge.

A concrete problem is that Restart as new with a non-zero prefix would fail on a
node that didn't store the journal entries in the journal v2 table.

Moreover, when rolling back to the previous version (where we are reading from
journal v1 first), there is the situation in which the invocation task would hang.
The problem is that the InvokerStorageReaderTransaction wouldn't read the journal
entries of an unpinned invocation that has an associated journal v2  because it
would only try to read the journal v1.

subject: Fence retry timers in the invoker to avoid panics and incorrect state transitions
body:
This commit fixes #4064 by replacing the TimerQueue with tokio_util::DelayQueue
for retry timer management in the invoker, and introducing a fencing mechanism
to prevent stale timers from causing panics or incorrect state transitions.

Problem
-------
The invoker could experience panics and incorrect behavior when retry timers
fired after the invocation state machine (ISM) had already transitioned to a
different state. Orphaned timers from previous retry cycles could fire and
trigger assertions or invalid state transitions.

Solution
--------
1. Replaced restate-timer-queue with tokio_util::DelayQueue: The new
   implementation uses DelayQueue which provides a Key for each inserted timer,
   enabling precise timer cancellation and identification.

2. Added timer fencing via RetryTimerKey: Each WaitingRetry state now stores
   the key of its associated retry timer. When a timer fires, the ISM verifies
   the key matches before reacting - stale timers are silently ignored.

3. Explicit timer cancellation: When an ISM transitions out of WaitingRetry
   state (via abort, pause, partition removal, or retry-now), the pending timer
   is explicitly cancelled using try_remove().

4. Refactored handle_task_error: The method now accepts a closure to register
   the timer, ensuring the timer key is captured at creation time and stored in
   the ISM state.

Key changes
-----------
- Removed restate-timer-queue dependency from restate-invoker-impl
- Added tokio-util with time feature for DelayQueue
- notify_retry_timer_fired() now takes a RetryTimerKey and validates it
- Added take_retry_timer_key() to retrieve the timer key from WaitingRetry state
- Periodic compaction of the DelayQueue every 10 seconds to reclaim memory
- Renamed OnTaskError::ScheduleRetry to OnTaskError::Retrying
- Updated all tests to use the new timer registration pattern

subject: [19/N] Refactor SchedulerClock to use WallClock
body:
Replace the custom time tracking mechanism in SchedulerClock with the centralized
WallClock from restate-clock crate. The previous approach used a datum (origin timestamp)
plus elapsed time from a tokio::Instant, which had two issues:
1. Clock drift: the scheduler clock could drift from wall time over long uptimes
2. Suspend/sleep blindness: tokio/std Instant does not account for system suspend or
   sleep time, causing the scheduler to fall behind after the system resumes

The new implementation uses WallClock::recent_us() which is updated by the upkeep thread
and properly tracks wall clock time.

Changes:
- SchedulerClock now uses WallClock::recent_us() for the gardal::Clock trait, with
  a fallback to WallClock::now_us() when the upkeep thread is not running (e.g., tests)
- Removed the millis_to_future_instant() method; callers now use duration_since() directly
- Added duration_since() methods to MillisSinceEpoch and NanosSinceEpoch for convenience
- Removed unused UniqueTimestamp::milliseconds_since() and as_secs_f64() methods
- Simplified check_eligibility() and poll_eligibility() to get time internally

NOTE: If we need tests with tight control over the scheduler clock, we can add a mock
clock later, but that is not included in this change.
